analysis:
The change to docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation only. The patch excerpt shows a scheduler-geometry table (head lines ~1087-1090): Gemma 4 gets a 2048 prefill chunk and 4096 step budget, other families keep 512/2048, the solo stripe is reworded, and a `bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling` of 512 is added. The range map also lists head ranges at 1101-1159 and 2041-2060. The supplied base units cover only base lines 798-1627, and the later head ranges were not visible, so I could not examine them. The base units describe the deadline, calibration, MTP, sampling and prefix-cache mechanics that the new table sits beside.

No control is weakened in the visible text. Memory-validated scheduling, KV reservations, first-content deadlines and the per-engine maxWaiting of 64 are unchanged. The prefix-cache and T-041 properties (HMAC-keyed lookup tags, 30-minute sliding TTL, coordinator-authored cacheSalt) are unchanged in the base text. The excerpt says nothing about media requests being excluded from prefix lookup, which is stated at base line 805. The documented behavior does change prefill geometry: a wider chunk for Gemma 4 raises per-step memory and latency, and the media chunk is capped at 512. This is performance and availability territory (T-010, T-029), and the visible doc keeps the existing admission and memory checks. Whether the wider chunk and step interact with the memory-validated scheduler projection and the evalLock contention described at base lines 1039-1046 is an implementation question for the Swift code, which is not supplied here. This is a doc-only change, so I record it as an unverified contract.

The visible changes are low-risk. The threat model needs no update for the visible edits, but the head-side ranges 1101-1159 and 2041-2060 should be checked for security-relevant claims (deadline, cache or attestation statements) in a later pass.
